context.scope: Qualified event-invoke stored configuration, runtime entry and successful destination boundaries; four owned SQS queues, execution role only sqs:SendMessage; no logs grants, concurrency reservation, retries experiment or metrics.
context.serialization: SDK blobs base64; invocation Payload JSON text; output Payload decoded. Native timestamps, request IDs, states and pagination tokens retained; account IDs normalized.

source: Native AWS boto3 authenticated SDK calls; credentials held in memory only; bounded requests with total_max_attempts=1

artifacts.source:
import json,time,os,uuid,boto3
from botocore.config import Config
BOOT=uuid.uuid4().hex
COUNT=0
DEPLOYMENT='initial'
sqs=boto3.client("sqs",config=Config(connect_timeout=3,read_timeout=5,retries={"total_max_attempts":1}))
def handler(event,context):
 global COUNT
 COUNT+=1
 result={"kind":"runtime-entry","deployment":DEPLOYMENT,"boot_id":BOOT,"boot_count":COUNT,"function_version":context.function_version,"invoked_function_arn":context.invoked_function_arn,"request_id":context.aws_request_id,"event":event,"started_at":time.time()}
 sqs.send_message(QueueUrl=os.environ["MARKER_QUEUE"],MessageBody=json.dumps(result))
 return result

interruption.cause: Shared eval Python globals collided with sibling capture before this capture created a Lambda function. Setup failed; its finally used the overwritten queue mapping and successfully deleted the sibling marker queue before encountering a mapping error. The sibling was notified, and its interrupted run was discarded as behavior evidence. This capture recovered only its exact originally owned qscope resources and reran in an isolated subprocess. Interrupted observations are setup/incident/recovery evidence only, never Lambda behavior evidence.

documentation.relevance: Configuration can be stored on a function, version or alias; Put replaces whereas Update preserves omitted settings. This page does not establish a propagation deadline or an inheritance algorithm.
Scope-specific lookup and qualified FunctionName/separate Qualifier request forms.
Replace semantics and qualified configuration ownership.
Partial updates to a configured scope.
Function-wide listing and opaque native pagination.
Unweighted FunctionVersion accepts $LATEST; verified by real runtime/destination controls.

reference_evidence.use: Read-only precursor: a fresh version configured before first async use delivered in both ARN forms while an unconfigured alias reached runtime without a destination in the earlier bounded window. This capture adds distinguishable destinations, paired positive controls and explicit warm/redeployment boundaries.

findings.observed: Unqualified Put created the :$LATEST configuration, retrievable with explicit $LATEST and full ARN. :1, :live and :latest stored distinct settings; aliases without their own config and :2 returned ResourceNotFoundException rather than parent configuration. Deleting explicit $LATEST removed the unqualified lookup too.

Fresh unqualified/$LATEST, direct :1, alias :live->1 and alias :latest->$LATEST each produced actual successful destinations on their configured queues. Full-ARN and separate-Qualifier requests both reached runtime and delivered for each configured qualified scope. Runtime markers and returned destination payloads identify deployment, executed version, invocation ARN, request ID, boot UUID and boot invocation counter.

Fresh :bare->1 with no alias config reached runtime but delivered to none of the three destination queues while both :1 and unqualified configs had paired successful delivery controls. :barelatest->$LATEST and unconfigured :2 likewise reached runtime with no destination. Repeating all three through full ARNs gave the same bounded outcome. After redeployment, fresh :newbare->3 again had a marker and no destination while :3 and :newlive->3 delivered to distinct configured destinations. These are bounded observations, not a universal timing or inheritance guarantee.

All four Update calls and immediate Get readbacks showed the new destinations. Warm unqualified and :1 entries 1.673s and 1.484s after their Update responses still delivered to OLD destinations. Warm :live and :latest entries 1.317s and 1.137s after their Update responses already delivered to NEW destinations. At 41.195s and 41.007s after the unqualified/:1 Update responses, the next entries delivered to NEW destinations using the same boot UUIDs as the earlier calls. Thus runtime restart was not required in this run, while successful API/readback alone did not mark immediate application for every scope. No per-scope propagation algorithm or fixed deadline is inferred.

Deleting :live, :1 (full-ARN form) and :latest configs returned HTTP 204, their Gets returned ResourceNotFoundException, and List retained only :$LATEST. Nevertheless a warm :live entry 1.264s after Delete response still delivered to its former destination. The simultaneous :1 and :latest entries had markers and no destinations. A later :live entry 53.046s after Delete response reused the same boot UUID and had no destination during the redeployed window; unqualified and fresh configured version/alias controls delivered. Stored deletion therefore was not an instantaneous delivery boundary for the measured alias.

Updating function code created new boot UUIDs for $LATEST and its alias. The redeployed unqualified request delivered to its updated destination; deleted-config :latest reached the new runtime without a destination. New published :3 and :newlive were configured before first use and each delivered to its distinct configured destination. No original published-version code was changed.

Put on :newlive with only MaximumRetryAttempts=1 removed its age field and destination, returning empty OnSuccess/OnFailure objects. Update adding age=66 preserved retry=1 and empty destinations. Update on an existing alias lacking a config returned 404; it did not create a config. Delete on an unconfigured alias also returned 404. Put on a nonexistent version and Update on a nonexistent alias returned 404 with native messages retained.

ListFunctionEventInvokeConfigs rejected full FunctionName ARNs qualified with :1, :live or :$LATEST, HTTP 400 InvalidParameterValueException: The function name must not include a version number or alias. MaxItems=1 on the unqualified function traversed four pages in native observed order live, 1, $LATEST, latest, with opaque NextMarker inputs/outputs retained and no terminal marker. Invalid Marker returned HTTP 400 InvalidParameterValueException: Invalid pagination key. The observed order is not asserted as a sorting contract.

limitations: All destination absence statements are limited to the recorded bounded SQS settlement windows (35 or 40 seconds requested, with the last bounded round allowed to finish). All queues were also read in subsequent windows until cleanup; no later matching destinations were observed. A runtime-entry marker proves entry and successful marker send, not by itself eventual handler completion or non-delivery forever.

The handler emits a marker and immediately returns; only actual successful destination records independently establish completion. No metrics, general retry behavior, failure destinations, tag authorization or admission-time configuration snapshot semantics were measured.

Observed old versus new destinations after hot changes establish non-instantaneous application and successful warm application in this sample, not a fixed cache duration, global propagation SLA or undocumented selection algorithm.

Configuration Put replacement and partial Update field preservation were measured at the stored API layer after the final delivery window; no claim is made about runtime application of those final field-only operations.
